issues.description: The Milkable.messageOnMilk method signature is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement and the template Main expect messageOnMilk() with no parameters, but the solution defines Milkable.messageOnMilk(double volume) (and Goat/Seal implement this variant). This prevents the template Main (and students following the spec) from compiling or matching the intended API and contradicts the textual specification that the method should return "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" with no volume parameter.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Milkable API consistent with the problem statement and template: change the solution's Milkable interface to declare messageOnMilk() with no parameters (returning String) and update Seal and Goat implementations to implement messageOnMilk() returning the string "[Animal Type] [name] is milked". Alternatively, if the volume parameter is intentional, update the problem statement and template Main to require and pass a volume parameter when calling messageOnMilk.

issues.description: The helper method singFarmSongVerse is declared differently in the template and the solution: the template defines private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/) (i.e., no formal parameter present) whereas the solution implements private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) and the UML/problem statement expects singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal). The commented-out parameter in the template can confuse students about the intended signature and prevents a straightforward implementation following the UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template Farm.java to declare singFarmSongVerse with the Animal parameter (private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)) to match the UML and the solution. Ensure singFarmSong() iterates over the farm's animals and calls singFarmSongVerse(animal). If the commented parameter was intentional as a placeholder, replace it with the proper signature to avoid confusion.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a Milkable.messageOnMilk() method with no parameters that returns a string like "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" (see UML and Part 2). However, the solution defines the Milkable interface and its implementations with a different signature messageOnMilk(double volume) and include the volume in the returned string (e.g., "Seal X is milked (1.0L)"). This mismatch in method signature and expected return format creates a mapping/confusion for students: the template's Main uses m.messageOnMilk() with no argument, but the solution's API requires a double parameter. This is an unintended identifier/signature inconsistency that will prevent straightforward implementation and testing.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Milkable API consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) change the solution to match the problem/template by using String messageOnMilk() with implementations returning "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" (no volume), or (B) update the problem statement and template to require messageOnMilk(double volume) and adjust the described return value to include the volume. Prefer option (A) to align with the UML and template usage.
